decisions.question: Approve or revise the README BLUF for the Bearing Delivery Lifecycle.
decisions.why_owner: The README is the owner-designated public source document, so its top-level product promise cannot be inferred from stale repository wording.

decisions.decision: README BLUF: Bearing Lite gives AI-assisted repository work a structured delivery lifecycle from an owner-approved plan to an independently assessed result. It improves repeatability and reduces hallucination risk through bounded implementation, deterministic checks, verification, validation, independent assurance, and traceable evidence. The following reviewability statement explains that planning artifacts and the Definition of Done Manifest compare what AI was authorized to touch with actual changes, supporting evidence, and unresolved gaps.

Planning uses one initial specialist pass plus at most one targeted reconciliation pass. The targeted pass includes every affected specialist concurrently; deterministic mismatches do not consume it, and remaining material conflict returns to the owner.
decisions.source: Owner approval after Grok Build efficiency review

decisions.decision: Architectural Alignment uses a deterministic existing-architecture extract by default. If no architecture exists or evidence does not cover the affected scope, record that gap, establish minimum system context from repository facts and owner intent, and activate Systems Modeler rather than inventing architecture.
decisions.source: Owner approval after Grok Build efficiency review

decisions.decision: Use one frozen shared planning frame, compact frame-plus-delta handoffs, deterministic coverage and trace checks before model redispatch, and a mechanical Plan Integrator that assembles agreed outputs without reopening specialist analysis.
decisions.source: Owner approval after Grok Build efficiency review

decisions.decision: Every planned change carries documentation impact, affected paths or discoverability status, responsible task, update timing, and verification. Unresolved documentation impact blocks planning approval unless marked not_applicable with evidence; documentation is updated and checked before final system assessment and projected in the DoD Manifest.

decisions.question: Approve the responsibility split for the initial planning frame: Orchestrator extracts facts and runs deterministic completeness checks; Requirements Engineer gates new or changed acceptance statements when applicable; Planning Integration Engineer owns compatibility, assembly-order, interface-risk, and integration judgments.
decisions.why_owner: This split controls planning speed and prevents the Orchestrator from silently assuming specialist engineering authority.
decisions.evidence_ref: DEC-BDL-012 through DEC-BDL-014; Grok Build efficiency review

decisions.decision: For the initial planning frame, Orchestrator extracts repository facts and runs deterministic structural checks; Requirements Engineer conditionally gates new or changed acceptance statements; Planning Integration Engineer owns compatibility, assembly-order, interface-risk, and integration judgments.

Planning review uses one independent review, at most one aggregated repair, deterministic closure, and no automatic rereview. The Orchestrator coordinates the transition and never becomes the reviewer.

Orchestrator checks planning readiness and receipt structure, not technical quality or implementation-evidence sufficiency. NEEDS_MORE_EVIDENCE is classified once and never automatically triggers another model or reviewer call; discoverable facts receive at most one bounded lookup.

Bounded uncertainty about whether a specified approach will work may enter implementation as a typed discovery task. Unresolved scope, interface contract, security boundary, acceptance intent, or owner authority remains a planning blocker even when downstream assurance might detect the problem.

decisions.question: When an implementation discovery result invalidates an approved plan claim, must it always stop dependent work and return to the human owner rather than automatically restarting a planning specialist?
decisions.why_owner: This determines whether discovery can reopen planning automatically and therefore whether the Orchestrator can enter a hidden replan loop.
decisions.evidence_ref: DEC-BDL-018; DEC-BDL-019; Grok Build lifecycle-control review

decisions.decision: An implementation discovery result that invalidates an approved plan claim stops dependent work and returns to the human owner. Specialists may be informed, but no specialist or Orchestrator may automatically restart planning or authorize a replacement plan.
decisions.source: Owner approval after Grok Build lifecycle-control review

decisions.question: When a required planning role and its approved fallbacks are unavailable, must planning stop for owner resolution rather than proceeding with a typed product capability gap?

decisions.decision: Add no separate unavailable-planning-role rule. A required role exhausted without a valid bounded receipt already fails the planning-readiness precondition and cannot transition; use the existing typed wait or owner-resolution path rather than duplicate policy.

decisions.why_owner: The slim initial integration frame deliberately defers these details, so their final authorship must be explicit to prevent omission or duplicate judgment.
decisions.evidence_ref: DEC-BDL-012 through DEC-BDL-016; Grok Build efficiency review

decisions.decision: After Systems Modeler and Planning Test Engineer return, Planning Integration Engineer finalizes anomaly handling, rollback, recovery, and integration V&V handoffs; Planning Test Engineer binds the corresponding proof cases; Plan Integrator copies the agreed outputs mechanically without adding judgment.

decisions.question: Approve the fallback continuity receipt: lifecycle/stage and frozen-frame identity; role objective and authority; settled decisions and completed work; artifact refs and changed paths; open blocker and remaining action; attempts and hypotheses already spent; verification commands/results; route/fallback reason and stop conditions. The fallback continues the same pass and budget without raw conversation history.
decisions.why_owner: A stable compact receipt lets an approved fallback resume safely without duplicate work, hidden authority expansion, or resetting the one-plus-one planning budget.
decisions.evidence_ref: DEC-BDL-012; DEC-BDL-018; DEC-BDL-021; owner fallback-continuity direction

decisions.decision: Create no continuation receipt. A resumed or fallback agent reads the existing journey.json and workspace.md contracts, then its active role contract and current task, and trusts accepted stages and confirmed decisions unless a bounded identity or drift check fails.

Before resuming or dispatching a fallback, Orchestrator performs one quick procedural preflight: check whether the prior agent/session is still active, read the current task state, compare current candidate/HEAD and scoped working changes with the last durable state, and classify RUNNING, COMPLETED, INACTIVE, or UNKNOWN. RUNNING is never duplicated; COMPLETED advances only from durable evidence; INACTIVE resumes from the last durable state without replay; UNKNOWN follows the configured liveness policy.

decisions.question: When the quick resume preflight returns UNKNOWN because the host exposes no reliable session status, should Orchestrator wait only for the role's configured liveness timeout and then permit fallback from durable state, without a global fixed timeout or model polling?
decisions.why_owner: UNKNOWN must avoid both duplicate concurrent work and indefinite waiting while remaining portable across hosts with different liveness surfaces.

decisions.decision: Bearing Lite does not depend on run-watchdog, a daemon, heartbeat service, global timeout, or model polling. Resume preflight queries the dispatched session or process once through the host-native surface. RUNNING is not duplicated; EXITED resumes with an approved fallback; COMPLETED advances only from durable evidence; UNKNOWN plus explicit owner-requested resume permits replacement, while automatic orchestration returns WAITING_ON.

decisions.question: Should reliable host-native session waiting and status inspection be a required capability for Orchestrator and Coordinator routes, with a route ineligible for those roles unless its wrapper supplies that capability?
decisions.why_owner: The owner observes that Claude and Astra wait reliably while Sol often struggles; encoding the need as a capability keeps core policy provider-neutral and prevents model behavior from controlling dispatch safety.

decisions.decision: Reliable session waiting and status inspection is advisory, not a required route capability. Public guidance states that wait/status reliability varies by host and route, recommends host-native status checks when available, and preserves safe RUNNING/EXITED/COMPLETED/UNKNOWN handling without excluding users who lack expensive models or advanced wrappers. Provider-specific observations remain private lineup evidence.

Orchestrator actively identifies and concurrently dispatches all ready, dependency-satisfied, proven-independent tasks within host concurrency and shared-resource limits. Dependencies, unresolved interfaces, overlapping writes, or shared mutable resources preserve ordering.
decisions.source: Owner direction refined through scheduling discussion

decisions.decision: Implementation has exactly two development strategies recorded in implementation.json: single_implementer is the speed-focused default and one Implementer writes product changes plus tests; tdd is explicitly selected by the owner or approved plan and orders Test Implementer before Product Implementer. There is no parallel Test Implementer/Product Implementer mode for one feature. Independent tasks may still run concurrently.

README includes an onboarding section and the advisory: Some agent harnesses may stall after delegated work completes. Before restarting the task, check whether the assigned agent is still active and avoid duplicate dispatch. Per-Lifecycle development strategy belongs in implementation.json rather than the global lineup catalog.

implementation.json carries role-specific assurance_cadence values from the closed enum slice, phase, or lifecycle. Defaults are phase for Assurance Test Engineer, phase for Reviewer, and lifecycle for Implementation Integration Engineer. Planning review remains separate.

Planning and Design defines a verification-ready contract for every slice. Observable behavior is defined whenever applicable, regardless of TDD mode; non-behavioral work uses the applicable analysis, inspection, demonstration, test, or evaluation contract; behavior that is genuinely unknown becomes a bounded discovery task rather than an invented contract.

decisions.decision: The sole persistent Bearing user configuration is ~/.agents/bearing-lite/profiles.json. Remove repository and user lineups.json plus default-role-lineup.md from active distribution and discovery. Runtime and skills never search, merge, prefer, or fall back to lineups.json; profiles.json owns named role assignments, ordered fallbacks, development strategy, planning review, assurance cadence, concurrency preferences, defaults, and owner holds.

Existing installations return MIGRATION_REQUIRED until an explicit deterministic migration validates lineups.json, writes and validates semantically equivalent profiles.json, and removes lineups.json. New installations expose only profiles.json; normal runtime never reads the old path.

Migration is a direct replacement across existing product surfaces: preserve skill, hook, template, test, README, and example behavior while replacing lineups/default-role-lineup terminology, paths, schema names, and fields with profiles equivalents. Remove the obsolete configuration files, not the product content that referred to them.

Do not add a separate slice-contract kind enum. Every implementation slice carries resolvable requirement or owner-decision, design, model when applicable, interface when applicable, and SEIT references. Observable behavior fields are required only when behavior changes; non-behavioral work uses its SEIT-selected V&V method; unknown behavior is bounded discovery. Plan Integrator projects accepted sources and cannot invent slice behavior.

decisions.decision: profiles.json configures deterministic-verification backend availability and user-specific settings, including optional Reverify. Backend availability does not select it for every task; Planning Test Engineer selects Reverify on an applicable binary-level SEIT claim, and implementation.json freezes that effective selection for the Lifecycle.

Retain issue 87 role use under the new names: Planning Test Engineer defines applicable deterministic claims and evidence; Planning Integration Engineer defines binary/configuration identity and checkpoints; Plan Integrator reconciles without inventing V&V; Implementer and Light Implementer may emit diagnostic evidence; Assurance Test Engineer runs planned assurance checks on the stable candidate; Reviewer may use Reverify to adjudicate a specific suspected defect; Orchestrator routes and records but never treats a backend as a role; post-repair deterministic closure adds no review round.

Execution Integration Engineer is not removed. It is the implementation-stage Integration Engineer that replaces Surveyor under issue 89. ATE assembles/configures approved elements and performs planned verification; Execution Integration Engineer then independently performs final system-level validation and integrated technical assessment against the approved user-facing outcome, at Lifecycle completion by default or an explicitly configured boundary.

Add a reusable onboard-bearing skill for first-run setup and explicit configuration reset. It creates or updates profiles.json, configures named role routes and fallbacks, development strategy, planning review, assurance cadence, concurrency preferences, holds, and optional deterministic-verification backends including Reverify; validates backend availability; migrates obsolete lineup configuration; previews destructive reset or replacement; writes atomically; validates readback; and stores no credentials.

Supersede DEC-BDL-039 reset wording. onboard-bearing is a reusable guided configuration skill. It inspects profiles.json when present, asks about profile settings one at a time, may recommend but never selects or writes a setting without the user's explicit instruction, preserves every unaddressed existing value, configures optional Reverify only when selected, validates the resulting profile, writes explicitly chosen changes atomically, and stores no credentials. Do not add a separate reset mode or explain reset semantics.

The versioned Definition of Done Manifest template uses the approved nine-section order: BLUF/state; identity; outcome/scope/DoD; requirements/architecture/design/interfaces/views; development strategy/task graph/roles/dependencies/write sets; V&V/cadence/evidence/status; documentation impact; risks/gaps/exceptions/anomaly/rollback/recovery; and authority/decisions/approvals/closeout. Non-applicable sections remain visible with a reason, and deterministic rendering preserves the same structure and visual system across agents.

Package the existing prompt skill with Bearing Lite unchanged. It remains an agnostic bounded-agent-handoff utility and is not adapted, renamed, or coupled to Bearing Lifecycle terminology, role names, providers, or harnesses.

The Definition of Done Manifest replaces review.html entirely. Its structured rendering input lives in implementation.json.dod_manifest so the canonical five-artifact package remains technical plan, design, seit.json, implementation.json, and <plan-name>-dod-manifest.html; no additional manifest instance artifact is created.

The DoD Manifest presents requirements and acceptance, design and interfaces, SEIT cases/evidence, and implementation.json tasks as fixed human-readable tables rather than raw JSON or prose dumps. Source artifacts remain agent-usable authorities; table rows retain stable IDs, source references, status, and trace links for human review.

Issue 88 uses a versioned fixed HTML template plus a small Node.js standard-library renderer. The renderer consumes implementation.json.dod_manifest, controls structure, escaping, tables, navigation, computed status, asset embedding, accessibility, responsive/print CSS, version identity, deterministic formatting, and output naming; it never authors semantics. A check mode rerenders and compares the expected output.

The DoD Manifest includes system and architecture models as a human-readable model inventory table and embedded rendered views. Each model/view retains stable ID, modeling mode, source artifact, revision/digest, stakeholder question or viewpoint, requirement/interface trace links, limitations, and render status. Systems Modeler owns semantics and prepared views; the renderer only validates and embeds them. A non-applicable model section remains visible with a reason, while a selected/required missing or stale view fails rendering visibly.

Integration Engineer is one role with separate planning and execution sessions, not separate Planning/Implementation/Execution Integration Engineer roles. Its planning session owns integration planning; its execution session replaces Surveyor and owns final system-level validation and integrated technical assessment. Test Engineer is likewise one role with planning and assurance sessions; Assurance Test Engineer names the assurance session, not a separate role. Profiles, diagrams, skills, schemas, task assignments, cadence keys, and public documentation must preserve these role/session relationships.

For DoD Manifest model views, prefer sanitized inline SVG when the modeling tool provides it and use embedded PNG as fallback. The canonical SysML model remains the semantic authority; the rendered image is a digest-bound human projection.

profiles.json uses nested role/session activation and routing. Systems Modeler has a planning session; Test Engineer has planning and assurance sessions; Integration Engineer has planning and execution sessions. Each session can be explicitly enabled or disabled during onboard-bearing, and cadence keys attach to test_engineer.assurance, reviewer, and integration_engineer.execution while preserving one role identity.

DoD Manifest closeout is append-only over the owner-approved planning projection. It preserves planned outcome, scope, exclusions, behavior, requirements, design, model references, tasks, DoD criteria, V&V plan, documentation impact, risks, recovery, and authority; it adds actual candidate, changed paths, completion status, evidence/results, documentation completion, anomalies/repairs/recovery used, residual gaps/risks, and closeout/owner-acceptance status. Changing planning content requires an explicit owner-approved plan amendment.

DoD Manifest adoption is forward-only. Do not migrate or otherwise spend scope on completed historical review.html artifacts. New Lifecycle outputs use the DoD Manifest; historical evidence remains historical without additional compatibility work in this Lifecycle.

Final issue 89 decision: remove the Surveyor skill and Surveyor from profiles, templates, schemas, hooks, tests, diagrams, and README; retain one Integration Engineer role with planning and execution sessions; move Surveyor outcome-assessment responsibility into integration_engineer.execution; and during configuration migration onboard-bearing asks the user which route to assign to the Integration Engineer execution session rather than choosing automatically. Do not reopen issue 89 owner decisions.

During onboard-bearing, ask whether the user wants Reverify. If selected but unavailable, ask whether to download and install it; download only after explicit approval, verify the installed source/version, then record enabled true. If the user declines Reverify or declines its download, persist reverify enabled false in that named profile and do not ask again during ordinary Lifecycles. A later explicit onboard-bearing configuration change may revisit the setting. No value is preselected.

Use the AGY DoD Manifest prototype as a strong visual baseline subject to final comparison. Improve accessibility coloring and replace pure-white screen backgrounds with a softer warm off-white or muted blue-gray surface to reduce eye strain while maintaining verified text, UI, and focus contrast. Status meaning remains redundant in text, symbols, shapes, and borders; print may use white for clarity and ink efficiency.
